In China&apos;s retail-dominated CSI 300 index (2005--2025), a one-standard-deviation increase in daily MRI predicts a 0.21 percentage point decrease in next-day excess returns (t=-4.71). The effect survives flexible controls for nonlinear momentum and volatility, and a 500-draw random-anchor placebo test confirms that the crash-detection algorithm is essential (p<0.002). In the U.S. S&P 500, however, MRI has no incremental predictive power and is spanned by VIX and valuation ratios.
